measure: a running or cumulative total over an ordering
gold_sql:
WITH filtered_measurements AS (
  SELECT
    apm.measurement_id,
    apm.allele_id,
    apm.peptide_id,
    apm.measurement_value,
    apm.experiment_date,
    a.allele_name,
    p.sequence AS peptide_sequence
  FROM allele_peptide_measurements AS apm
  JOIN alleles AS a
    ON apm.allele_id = a.allele_id
  JOIN peptides AS p
    ON apm.peptide_id = p.peptide_id
  WHERE apm.measurement_value IS NOT NULL
    AND apm.measurement_value > (
      SELECT AVG(measurement_value)
      FROM allele_peptide_measurements
      WHERE measurement_value IS NOT NULL
    )
),
ranked_measurements AS (
  SELECT
    allele_name,
    peptide_sequence,
    measurement_value,
    experiment_date,
    SUM(measurement_value) OVER (
      PARTITION BY allele_name
      ORDER BY experiment_date, measurement_id
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS running_total,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY allele_name
      ORDER BY measurement_value DESC, measurement_id
    ) AS value_rank
  FROM filtered_measurements
),
survivors AS (
  SELECT
    allele_name,
    peptide_sequence,
    measurement_value,
    running_total
  FROM ranked_measurements
  WHERE value_rank <= 3
)
SELECT
  allele_name,
  COUNT(*) AS surviving_measurement_count,
  MAX(running_total) AS final_running_total,
  AVG(measurement_value) AS average_surviving_measurement_value
FROM survivors
GROUP BY allele_name
ORDER BY final_running_total DESC, allele_name
question: For each HLA allele, consider only peptide-binding measurements whose numeric measurement value is above the overall average measurement value across all measurements with non-null values. Among those, keep the three measurements with the highest measurement values for that allele, and report the allele name, the number of retained measurements, the final cumulative total of measurement values when that allele’s retained set is accumulated in experiment-date order, and the average measurement value of the retained measurements. Order the results by the final cumulative total in descending order, breaking ties by allele name.

gate.row_grain: One row per HLA allele that has qualifying peptide-binding measurements
columns: final cumulative total of measurement values
average measurement value of retained measurements
gate.why: The question asks for specific per-allele aggregated metrics calculated over up to three top peptide-binding measurements exceeding the overall average value.

measure: a change or difference between two periods
gold_sql:
WITH period_access AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN al.access_date < '2024-01-01' THEN 'prior_period'
      ELSE 'later_period'
    END AS period_label,
    COUNT(*) AS access_count
  FROM access_logs al
  JOIN digital_outputs do
    ON al.output_id = do.output_id
  JOIN output_storage os
    ON do.output_id = os.output_id
  WHERE al.access_date IS NOT NULL
    AND do.is_public = 1
    AND os.is_default = 1
    AND do.output_type IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY period_label
)
SELECT
  MAX(CASE WHEN period_label = 'later_period' THEN access_count END) -
  MAX(CASE WHEN period_label = 'prior_period' THEN access_count END) AS access_count_change
FROM period_access
question: Calculate the change in total access-event volume between the period before January 1, 2024 and the period on or after January 1, 2024 for digital outputs that are publicly accessible, have a default storage location, and have a defined output type. Count all access events with a non-null access date in each of the two periods, and report the later-period count minus the prior-period count as a single value.

gate.row_grain: A single numeric value representing the change in total access-event volume (later-period count minus prior-period count).
gate.why: The question explicitly requests a single calculated scalar value representing the difference between access-event counts in two specified time periods for digital outputs matching given criteria.

measure: a change or difference between two periods
gold_sql:
WITH gold_by_journal AS (
  SELECT
    journal_id,
    COUNT(*) AS gold_term_count,
    AVG(CAST(LENGTH(COALESCE(apc, '')) AS REAL)) AS avg_gold_apc_len,
    MIN(content_licence) AS min_gold_licence,
    MAX(content_licence) AS max_gold_licence
  FROM gold_oa_terms
  GROUP BY journal_id
),
green_by_journal AS (
  SELECT
    journal_id,
    COUNT(*) AS green_policy_count,
    AVG(CAST(COALESCE(embargo_period, 0) AS REAL)) AS avg_embargo_months,
    MIN(COALESCE(embargo_period, 0)) AS min_embargo_months,
    MAX(COALESCE(embargo_period, 0)) AS max_embargo_months
  FROM green_oa_policies
  GROUP BY journal_id
)
SELECT
  j.journal_id,
  j.title AS journal_title,
  COALESCE(gold_by_journal.gold_term_count, 0) AS gold_term_count,
  COALESCE(green_by_journal.green_policy_count, 0) AS green_policy_count,
  COALESCE(gold_by_journal.gold_term_count, 0) - COALESCE(green_by_journal.green_policy_count, 0) AS period_difference,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(green_by_journal.green_policy_count, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(gold_by_journal.gold_term_count, 0) AS REAL) / green_by_journal.green_policy_count, 3)
  END AS gold_to_green_ratio,
  ROUND(COALESCE(gold_by_journal.avg_gold_apc_len, 0), 2) AS avg_gold_apc_length,
  ROUND(COALESCE(green_by_journal.avg_embargo_months, 0), 2) AS avg_embargo_months,
  COALESCE(gold_by_journal.min_gold_licence, '') AS min_gold_licence,
  COALESCE(green_by_journal.max_embargo_months, 0) AS max_embargo_months
FROM journals AS j
LEFT JOIN gold_by_journal ON gold_by_journal.journal_id = j.journal_id
LEFT JOIN green_by_journal ON green_by_journal.journal_id = j.journal_id
ORDER BY period_difference DESC, j.journal_id
question: For every journal, compare its gold open-access terms with its green open-access policies. Show the journal ID, journal title, number of gold OA term records, number of green OA policy records, the difference between those two counts (gold minus green), the gold-to-green ratio based on those counts, the average character length of the gold OA article processing charge field, the average green OA embargo period in months, the alphabetically earliest gold content licence, and the maximum green OA embargo period; order the results by the count difference from largest to smallest, then by journal ID.

columns: number of gold OA term records
number of green OA policy records
difference between gold and green record counts (gold minus green)
average character length of the gold OA article processing charge field
average green OA embargo period in months
gate.why: The prompt unambiguously defines the grouping level (per journal), every calculation and metadata field to display, and the precise sort order.

measure: a per-unit rate (per day, per member, per km)
naive_sql:
SELECT
  p.paper_id,
  p.title,
  COUNT(r.review_id) * 1.0 / COUNT(c.conflict_id) AS reviews_per_conflict
FROM papers AS p
JOIN reviews AS r
  ON p.paper_id = r.paper_id
JOIN conflicts_of_interest AS c
  ON p.paper_id = c.paper_id
GROUP BY p.paper_id, p.title
ORDER BY p.paper_id
gold_sql:
WITH paper_review_counts AS (
  SELECT
    p.paper_id,
    p.title,
    COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count
  FROM papers AS p
  LEFT JOIN reviews AS r
    ON p.paper_id = r.paper_id
  GROUP BY p.paper_id, p.title
),
paper_conflict_counts AS (
  SELECT
    p.paper_id,
    COUNT(c.conflict_id) AS conflict_count
  FROM papers AS p
  LEFT JOIN conflicts_of_interest AS c
    ON p.paper_id = c.paper_id
  GROUP BY p.paper_id
)
SELECT
  prc.paper_id,
  prc.title,
  prc.review_count * 1.0 / NULLIF(pcc.conflict_count, 0) AS reviews_per_conflict
FROM paper_review_counts AS prc
JOIN paper_conflict_counts AS pcc
  ON prc.paper_id = pcc.paper_id
ORDER BY prc.paper_id

measure: an average or median of a per-row quantity
gold_sql:
WITH project_reviewers AS (
    SELECT
        fp.project_id,
        fp.application_id,
        fp.total_funding,
        a.reviewer_id
    FROM funded_projects AS fp
    JOIN applications AS a
        ON a.application_id = fp.application_id
    GROUP BY
        fp.project_id,
        fp.application_id,
        fp.total_funding,
        a.reviewer_id
),
reviewer_project_stats AS (
    SELECT
        pr.reviewer_id,
        COUNT(*) AS project_count,
        AVG(pr.total_funding) AS avg_funding_per_project
    FROM project_reviewers AS pr
    GROUP BY pr.reviewer_id
)
SELECT
    r.reviewer_id AS reviewer_id,
    r.reviewer_name AS reviewer_name,
    rps.project_count AS project_count,
    rps.avg_funding_per_project AS avg_funding_per_project
FROM reviewer_project_stats AS rps
JOIN reviewers AS r
    ON r.reviewer_id = rps.reviewer_id
ORDER BY rps.avg_funding_per_project DESC, r.reviewer_name

measure: a share of a total, computed against a window or subtotal
gold_sql:
WITH occupation_totals AS (
  SELECT
    o.occupation_name AS occupation_name,
    COUNT(*) AS total_individuals,
    SUM(CASE WHEN v.veteran_status_name = 'Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS veteran_individuals
  FROM individuals i
  JOIN occupations o
    ON i.occupation_id = o.occupation_id
  LEFT JOIN veteran_statuses v
    ON i.veteran_status = CAST(v.veteran_status_id AS TEXT)
  GROUP BY o.occupation_name
)
SELECT
  occupation_name,
  veteran_individuals,
  total_individuals,
  ROUND(1.0 * veteran_individuals / SUM(total_individuals) OVER (), 4) AS veteran_share_of_all_individuals
FROM occupation_totals
ORDER BY veteran_share_of_all_individuals DESC
